Fumaria officinalis: Arable land and as a weed in gardens, usually on lighter soils. It is also found growing on old walls.
Galeopsis tetrahit: Arable land, sometimes in woods, fens and wet heaths.
Galium aparine: Hedgerows and as a weed of cultivated land. Moist and grassy places on most types of soil.
Gentiana lutea: Grassy alpine and sub-alpine pastures, usually on calcareous soils.
Ginkgo biloba: Found wild in only 2 localities at Guizhou and on the Anhui/Zhejiang border, where it grows on rich sandy soils.
Glycyrrhiza glabra: Dry open places, especially in sandy places near the sea.
Grindelia robusta: By the coast in sunny well-drained situations. Thrives in dry areas and salty plains.
Gymnema sylvestre: Secondary forest, riverine forest and dry shrub savannah, usually on sandy or loamy soils. It occurs scattered and is locally abundant and common.
Gynostemma pentaphyllum: Thickets in open forests in lowland all over Japan. Forest, thickets or road sides on mountain slopes at elevations of 300 - 3200 metres in China.
Hamamelis virginiana: Edges of dry or moist woods, in rich soil and on the rocky banks of streams. The best specimens are found in deep rich soils.
Helichrysum arenarium: Dry sandy places, heaths, dunes, pine forests etc.
Humulus lupulus: Hedgerows, woodlands and sunny waste ground.
Hyacinthus orientalis: Among rocks, up to 2000 metres in Turkey
Hydrangea macrophylla: Sunny places near the coast of E. Japan.
Hydrastis canadensis: Rich shady woods and moist areas on woodland edges. Mesic, deciduous forests, often on clay soils at elevations of 50 - 1200 metres.
Hyoscyamus niger: By the walls of fields, waste ground, near buildings and in stony places from low-lying ground near the sea to lower mountain slopes.
Hypericum perforatum: Open woods, hedgebanks and grassland, in dry sunny places, usually on calcareous soils.
Hyssopus officinalis: Old walls and buildings, stony places. Dry hills and rock ledges to 2200 metres in Turkey.
Ilex paraguariensis: Grows primarily in seasonally dry tropical forest regions. An understorey tree of mixed Araucaria forest.
Inula helenium: Fields, waysides, waste places, copses etc, often on moist soils in shade.
Jasminum officinale: Shrubberies and forests, usually on humus-rich soils, 1200 - 3000 metres in the Himalayas. Valleys, ravines, thickets, woods, along rivers, meadows; 1800 - 4000 metres in W. China.
Juniperus communis: Chalk downs in S. England but only where there is least sunshine and most rain, heaths, moors, pine and birch woods in the north of Scotland on acid peat, often dominant on chalk, limestone and slate.
Lamium album: Fields, hedgerows, woodland edges and clearings and moist waste ground.
Laurus nobilis: Damp rocks and ravines, thickets and old walls.
Lavandula angustifolia: Dry grassy slopes amongst rocks, in exposed, usually parched, hot rocky situations often on calcareous soils.
Lavandula stoechas: Dry hills, garigue and open woods on limestone and granite soils.
Leonurus cardiaca: Hedge banks, waste places etc, usually on gravelly or calcareous soils.
Lilium candidum: Rocky slopes and in scrub to 600 metres.
Lycium barbarum: Hedges, on walls and waste ground.
Mahonia aquifolium: Mixed coniferous woods to 2000 metres. It is found in woods and hedgerows in Britain.
Malva sylvestris: Waste ground, field verges and roadsides, avoiding acid soils.
Matricaria chamomilla: Sandy or loamy arable soils in Britain. Also found on saline steppes in Europe.
Melissa officinalis: Waste places and derelict land near human habitations.
Mentha aquatica: Swamps, fen, marshes, near rivers, streams and ponds, in wet woods.
Mentha arvensis: Arable land, heaths, damp edges of woods.
Mentha piperita: A natural hybrid, M. aquatica x M. spicata found in moist soils on the sides of ditches, roadsides etc in S. England.
Mentha pulegium: Moist meadows and sandy soils by streams etc.
Mentha spicata: Roadsides and waste places, usually in damp soils and sunny positions.
Monstera deliciosa: An epiphytic vine, growing in the branches of trees in moist or wet, mountain forests at elevations of 900 - 1,500 metres.
Nasturtium officinale: Stream margins, ditches, flushes etc with moving water, usually in chalk or limestone areas.
Nepeta cataria: Roadsides and near streams. Hedgerows, borders of fields, dry banks and waste ground, especially on calcareous and gravelly soils.
Nigella sativa: Waste places, arable land and waysides.
Ocimum basilicum: Long cultivated, its original habitat is obscure.
Ocimum basilicum var. purpureum: Long cultivated, its original habitat is obscure.
Ocimum tenuiflorum: Naturalized in waste places or in settled areas and thickets.
Olea europaea: Woods and scrub in dry rocky places.
Origanum majorana: Dry slopes and rocky places, occasionally in partial shade, to 1500 metres in Turkey.
Origanum vulgare: Dry grassy areas and scrub, usually on calcareous soils.
Oxalis acetosella: Moist woods, moorland and on shady rocks.
Paeonia lactiflora: Dry open stony slopes, riverbanks and sparse woodland edges. Woods and grasslands at elevations of 400 - 2300 metres in China.
Passiflora incarnata: Sandy thickets and open soils. Fields, roadsides, fence rows and thickets.
Paullinia cupana: Tropical rainforest at elevations up to 800 metres.
Peganum harmala: Dry steppes, especially where grazing is heavy, and dry waste places. It is often found in saline soils.
Pelargonium graveolens: Near the Hex river in S.W. Cape province.
Pelargonium hortorum: Dry rocky hills, stony slopes and forest margins from the Southern Cape to Natal.
Petasites hybridus: Wet meadows and copses by streams to 1500 metres. The female form is rare or absent from much of Britain.
Petroselinum crispum: Grassy waste places on walls and rocks, especially on limestone and near the coast.
Phyllanthus emblica: Mixed forests. Drier forests. Dry open sparse forests or scrub, village groves at elevations of 200 - 2,300 metres in southern China.
Pimpinella anisum: Not known in a truly wild situation.
Pinus sylvestris: Forming woods in the mountains of Scotland.
Pistacia lentiscus: Open woods and scrub on dry hillsides, usually by the coast.
